sphere_commentary.overview:
Across the three series the Drum Protocols show broadly comparable efficacy with modest variation.
• HEALING yields a mean of 6.98, the largest sample (n=574) and relatively tight spread.
• THRIVING scores 6.96 on average, with the highest individual means in Focus & Clarity.
• TRANSFORMING averages 6.59, reflecting its design for low‑affect states and greater outcome variance.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series‑level patterns align with their intended therapeutic arcs.
• HEALING shows the most consistent listener responses, especially in Over‑stimulation and Anxiety blocks.
• THRIVING delivers the strongest peaks in Focus & Clarity and Creative Flow, albeit with higher variance.
• TRANSFORMING displays the widest spread, matching its ascending‑arc purpose for mood and motivation.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
A few protocols deviate from series trends, suggesting population or design mismatches.
• X-MC-L3 records a low mean (5.7) and high std (2.45) despite being a Mind & Clarity descent protocol.
• X-MD-L3 exhibits extreme cross‑run drift (sim=0.507) and a bimodal outcome distribution.
• H‑SL‑L1 and T‑FC‑L3 also show notable drift, flagging possible instability in qualitative commentary.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Targeted refinements could raise efficacy and discovery.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 – n=10, mean=5.7, std=2.45 – create an L2 variant with altered rhythm to improve accessibility.
• H-CR-L3 – n=27, mean=6.52, std=1.91 – experiment with a longer hold phase (≈+20%) to deepen entrainment for acute distress.
• T-MB-L2 – n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03 – stratify listener types to identify sub‑groups driving the high variance.
• H-OS-L1 – n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78 – boost promotional routing (e.g., adviser‑driven) to capitalize on strong but under‑exposed efficacy.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Embedding signals reveal evolving analytical framing and limited clustering.
• CROSS‑RUN DRIFT: 28 protocols show sim<0.85, indicating notable commentary instability across runs.
• CROSS‑PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: insufficient data for robust clustering; only one run available.
• Confidence note: drift metrics are reliable, but semantic cluster insights remain weak due to limited embedding volume.
